sources.title: A Theater Designed in the Egyptian Style, The Architect and Engineer, March 1923
observations: Meyer and Holler designed the theatre.
Elaborate painted decoration contrasts with deliberately plain wall surfaces.
Forecourt had shops on one side and palms and potted plants on the other.
Massive Egyptian colonnade precedes lobby; painted or carved hieroglyphic decoration at doors and vestibules.
sources.access: Web text inspected; local direct download rejected with HTTP 403. No reference artwork copied into textures.

sources.title: The Egyptian Theatre, Los Angeles Conservancy
observations: Institutional historic postcard shows red-tile roof above the central colonnade, forecourt shop awnings, broad unornamented courtyard, and palms along the opposing wall.

sources.title: 100th Anniversary of the Egyptian Theatre, Hollywood Heritage
observations: Historic entrance postcard shows thick cylindrical Egyptian columns and rectangular capital blocks, painted winged sun and figural wall motifs, red tile coping, and a strongly recessed dark doorway.

sources.title: Egyptian Theatre, Los Angeles Historic Theatre Foundation
observations: Restoration advocacy prioritizes original 1922 character and period courtyard gateways.
Modern lobby and neon additions should not be treated as original 1930 design evidence.

adaptation_notes: SPEC collision dimensions override the smaller historic courtyard proportions.
Large central dungeon doorway, wing colonnades and 30 m pylon gate are deliberate game adaptations mandated by SPEC, not measured historical reconstructions.
Main block uses a low red-tile entrance canopy and otherwise flat finished roof; no later tall neon tower or Netflix branding.
Original painted geometric Egyptian-inspired ornaments are texture instructions, not reproductions of photographic murals.
All photographs/postcards are read-only research references; texture-only endpoint receives newly generated concept artwork.
